title: How Many Days in Vis, Croatia: 2027 Planning Guide
metaDescription: How many days to spend in Vis: 2 nights is the sweet spot. Day-trip verdict, 7- and 10-day Croatia routes, ferry times, costs and advice by traveler type.
content:
## How Many Days Do You Need in Vis?

Two nights is the best answer for most visitors. Vis is the most remote of the inhabited central Dalmatian islands, and it was closed to foreigners until 1989 because of its military role. Because of that, it has little mass tourism and a quiet pace. A visit of less than 24 hours mostly uses up the time on boats. A stay longer than 4 nights suits only people who want a beach holiday or a base for island hopping.

This guide covers how long to stay and how Vis fits into a wider route. It is not a day-by-day itinerary.

## Getting to Vis: What Affects the Length of Your Stay

Travel time is the main factor in deciding how long to stay.

- **Fast catamaran (Kapetan Luka-Krilo):** about 1 h 10 min from Split, with tickets from about €10.
- **Jadrolinija car ferry:** about 2 h 20 min, roughly €8 per person on foot. A car costs much more.
- **Summer Jadrolinija catamaran (line 659, 19 June–13 September 2026):** Split to Vis €28 and Vis to Hvar €25 in high season. It calls at Milna on Brač and at Hvar on some sailings.
- **Private taxi boat:** about 65 min, from roughly €460 per boat. It makes sense only for groups.

Schedules change by season and some Jadrolinija services run only on certain weekdays. Check the timetable for your exact dates before booking. In winter, sailings are fewer and weather cancellations are more likely.

## What You Can See in 1 Day

One day on Vis is enough for a taste, not a stay. With the fast catamaran you arrive late morning and leave in the evening, if the timetable allows. Realistically that gives time for Vis Town and one swim, or a boat trip to the Blue Cave from Komiža. You cannot reasonably do both Vis Town and Komiža, and the Blue Cave in one day without a hire car or taxi.

The Blue Cave on Biševo is about 5 km southwest of Vis and 8.3 km by sea from Komiža. Boats take 15–20 minutes from Komiža. In 2026 the cave entrance fee was about €18 in shoulder season and €24 in peak season (from 20 June to 10 September), paid in cash on Biševo. There is no ATM on the island. Time inside the cave is short, usually 5–15 minutes. Queues can run past an hour in July and August.

## What You Can See in 2–3 Days

This is the recommended length. Two nights allows:

- One half day in Vis Town (Kut and Luka quarters, the waterfront).
- One half day in Komiža, the fishing town on the west side, about 12 km from Vis Town.
- One boat day for the Blue Cave and beaches on Biševo and Vis. Komiža operators run small-group speedboat tours. One operator lists the Blue Cave tour at €30 per adult, with the cave ticket extra. Prices for longer tours with bays and stops range from €35 to €70.
- A swim at Stiniva or Stončica.

**Opinion:** if you have only one night to give Vis, skip it and spend that time on Hvar or Brač. A single night yields mostly ferry time. Two nights is where the island starts to repay the trip.

## What a Longer Stay (4–7 Nights) Adds

Four or more nights suit beach holidays and slow travel. You can switch between Vis Town and Komiža, rent a scooter or small car, and visit quieter coves without a schedule. Wine is also a draw. The island grows local varieties such as Vugava (white) and Plavac (red), and small family cellars are open to visitors. Longer stays also let you wait out a windy day, which often cancels boat tours.

## Is Vis Worth a Day Trip From Split or Hvar?

A day trip works, but only with planning. From Split, the 1 h 10 min catamaran makes it possible if you catch the morning boat and return in the evening. The timetable and available seats decide this, and not every day has a convenient pair of sailings. Full-day group tours from Split to the Blue Cave typically cost €80–125 per person plus the cave fee, and they spend the day on a boat rather than on Vis. From Hvar, a day tour costs around €100 per person plus entrance.

**Local tip:** buy the cave ticket in advance through a tour operator if offered. Book the first tour slot of the morning to avoid the longest queues.

## How to Fit Vis Into a 7-Day Croatia Route

A 7-day trip works best with a Split base. A sample structure is 2 nights Dubrovnik, 1–2 nights Hvar or Korčula, 2 nights Vis and 2 nights Split. Another option is to skip Dubrovnik and use Split with Vis and Hvar as a three-stop Dalmatia trip. Vis takes 2 nights out of 7, so drop something else, such as a second Hvar night, rather than shortening Vis to one night.

## How to Fit Vis Into a 10-Day Croatia Route

Ten days gives room for a fuller plan: 2 nights Zagreb or Plitvice, 3 nights Split with Trogir or Krka, 2 nights Vis, 1–2 nights Hvar, 2 nights Dubrovnik. The summer catamaran from Vis to Hvar allows a triangle of Split, Vis, Hvar and back to Split without backtracking. The cost for the boats is about €45–60 per person. A 10-day trip can also support 3–4 nights on Vis if beaches are the priority.

## Which Time of Year Works Best?

June and September offer warm water, regular boats and smaller crowds than July and August. July and August bring the longest Blue Cave queues, with around 1,500 cave tickets sold a day at peak. Winter ferries run but fewer, and many restaurants and boat operators close.

## Recommendation by Traveler Type

- **First-timers to Croatia:** 2 nights if your trip is 10 days or longer. On a 7-day trip, skip Vis or visit on a day trip and prioritize Split, Hvar and Dubrovnik.
- **Families:** 2–3 nights. Short crossings are easiest with the fast catamaran, and children aged 3–12 pay reduced fares on some services. One boat trip is enough; the Blue Cave queue is hard on young children.
- **Couples:** 2–3 nights. Stay one night in each of Vis Town and Komiža. Visit the cave in shoulder season for a calmer experience.
- **Beach holiday:** 4–5 nights. Base in Vis Town or Komiža, hire a scooter or car, and mix pebble coves with boat days.

faq.question: How many days should I spend in Vis?
faq.answer: Two nights (three days) is the best fit for most travelers. It gives time for Vis Town, Komiža and a Blue Cave boat trip. Beach holidaymakers can extend to 4–5 nights.

faq.question: Can you visit Vis as a day trip from Split?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is tight. The fast catamaran takes about 1 h 10 min, with tickets from about €10. Check that the morning and evening sailings both run on your date.

faq.question: How long is the ferry from Split to Vis?
faq.answer: The fast catamaran takes about 1 h 10 min to 2 h depending on stops. The Jadrolinija car ferry takes about 2 h 20 min and costs around €8 per person on foot.

faq.question: Is one night enough in Vis?
faq.answer: One night is usually not enough. Most of the time is taken by the boat journey, and you can see only one of Vis Town, Komiža or the Blue Cave. Two nights is a better minimum.

faq.question: How much does the Blue Cave cost from Vis?
faq.answer: In 2026 the cave ticket was about €18 in shoulder season and €24 in peak season (20 June–10 September), paid in cash on Biševo. Speedboat tours from Komiža start around €30 per adult, with the ticket extra.

faq.question: Can Vis fit into a 7-day Croatia trip?
faq.answer: Yes, with 2 nights, if you base around Split and cut another stop. Without that, it is better to leave Vis for a longer trip.

quickAnswer: Spend 2 nights (3 days) in Vis. That is enough for Vis Town, Komiža, one beach day and a Blue Cave boat trip without rushing. A day trip from Split is possible but tight, since the fast catamaran takes about 1 h 10 min. Stay 4–5 nights only for a slow beach holiday.
